guides.title: Find water already in your house
guides.summary: Water heater tank, toilet tank (not bowl), ice, and canned liquid: how to get at it safely.

guides.title: How much water to store
guides.summary: At least 1 gallon per person per day for 3 days, 2 weeks if you can, in clean labeled containers.

guides.title: Make water safe by boiling
guides.summary: Rolling boil for 1 minute, then cool and store covered. Boiling kills germs, not chemicals.

guides.title: Make water safe with bleach
guides.summary: EPA drops per gallon for 6% and 8.25% bleach, plus cloudy water, wait time and the smell test.

guides.title: Portable water filters
guides.summary: What filters remove and don't, plus care for Sawyer, LifeStraw, Katadyn BeFree and Berkey.

guides.title: Water purification tablets
guides.summary: Chlorine dioxide and iodine tablets: contact times, limits and cautions. Follow your package.

guides.title: Which water can I use?
guides.summary: A table of water sources and the treatment each one needs. Some can't be made safe.

guides.title: Canned food and botulism
guides.summary: Which cans and jars to throw out, how to sanitize sealed cans after a flood, and botulism warning signs.

guides.title: Eating when the power is out
guides.summary: No-cook meals, what to eat first, and how to save fuel for the jobs that need a flame.

guides.title: Fridge and freezer in a power outage
guides.summary: Fridge 4 hours, full freezer 48 hours, half-full 24 hours. Check with a thermometer; when in doubt, throw it out.

guides.title: Butane camp stove safety
guides.summary: Outdoor use only for the stoves I checked: ventilation, pot size, canister heat limits, leaks and storage.

guides.title: Carbon monoxide: alarm and poisoning
guides.summary: If the CO alarm sounds: get outside, call 911, stay out. Never use grills, generators or camp stoves indoors.

guides.title: Propane stove and 1 lb cylinders
guides.summary: Outdoors only: connect, leak-test with soapy water, store away from heat, and keep CO out of the house.

guides.title: Keep phones and lights running
guides.summary: Low-power mode, power banks, safe car charging, and how to read battery capacity in watt-hours.

guides.title: Portable generator safety
guides.summary: Run it outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house. Never plug it into a wall outlet. Let it cool before refueling.

guides.title: Emergency bucket toilet
guides.summary: Line a toilet bowl or 5-gallon bucket with two bags, add an absorbent, tie off, store, and wash your hands.

guides.title: Handwashing, dishes and cleaning without running water
guides.summary: Wash with soap for 20 seconds, use 60% alcohol sanitizer only as a backup, and sanitize dishes with bleach.

guides.title: Boil-water advisory: what to do
guides.summary: Tap water may have germs. Boil it for 1 minute or use bottled water. Know the difference from a do-not-drink advisory.

guides.title: Evacuation and go-bag
guides.summary: When to leave, what to pack, and what to do before you lock the door. The T1D go-kit has its own guide.

guides.title: Extreme heat
guides.summary: Above 90°F for 2 to 3 days. Fans don't cool you above 95°F. Know heat stroke (above 103°F) and when to call 911.

guides.title: Hurricane and tropical storm
guides.summary: Watch means within 48 hours, warning within 36. Inland risks: wind, power loss, flash floods, tornadoes.

guides.title: Nuclear plant accident or fallout
guides.summary: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned. Potassium iodide (KI) protects only the thyroid, only if officials say to take it.

guides.title: Power outage
guides.summary: Before, during and after an outage: food, heat and cold, medical devices, generators, and downed lines.

guides.title: Tornado
guides.summary: Watch: be ready. Warning: take shelter now in the lowest interior room, away from windows. Mobile homes are not safe.

guides.title: Winter storm and ice
guides.summary: Ice takes down power lines. Stay warm safely, avoid CO, stay off roads, and watch for hypothermia and frostbite.

guides.title: Getting more insulin and supplies in a disaster
guides.summary: Pharmacist emergency refills under Virginia law, diabetes hotlines, what to keep copies of, and what to do if your usual insulin is gone.

guides.title: Insulin pump or pod failure
guides.summary: What to check first, why you need injections ready within hours, and the general approach pump makers and FDA describe.

guides.title: Keeping insulin safe without a fridge
guides.summary: How long insulin lasts at room temperature, what ruins it (freezing, heat), and how to keep it cool when the power is out.

guides.title: Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
guides.summary: Spot a low, treat it with the 15-15 rule, and know when it is a severe low that needs glucagon and 911.

guides.title: Sick days, ketones and DKA
guides.summary: Keep taking insulin, check glucose and ketones, drink fluids, and know the signs that mean go to the ER.

guides.title: Type 1 diabetes go-kit
guides.summary: A tickable checklist of what to pack so you can leave fast and still manage insulin, lows and sick days.

guides.title: Using glucagon for a severe low
guides.summary: How to give nasal Baqsimi, Gvoke (pen, syringe, kit), Zegalogue, or a traditional mix-it-yourself glucagon kit, and what to do after.

guides.title: When the CGM stops working
guides.summary: Switch to fingersticks, handle warm-up, signal loss and sensor errors on Dexcom and FreeStyle Libre, and know when not to trust a reading.

guides.title: Broken bones, sprains and strains
guides.summary: Keep the injury still, splint it, treat for shock, and know which injuries need 911.

guides.title: Burns
guides.summary: Cool a minor burn, cover it, and know which burns need 911.

guides.title: Choking: adults, children and infants
guides.summary: Back blows and abdominal thrusts for adults and children over 1; back blows and chest thrusts for babies under 1.

guides.title: Cuts and wounds: cleaning, closing, infection and tetanus
guides.summary: Clean a cut, when it needs stitches, infection signs to watch, and when a tetanus shot is due.

guides.title: Dehydration and oral rehydration solution
guides.summary: Signs of dehydration, the WHO recipe for a homemade rehydration drink, and when to get help.

guides.title: Hands-only CPR and AED (adults)
guides.summary: Call 911, push hard and fast in the center of the chest, and use an AED as soon as you have one. Training matters.

guides.title: Heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke
guides.summary: Tell the three apart, cool the person fast, and know that heat stroke is a 911 emergency.

guides.title: Home first-aid kit checklist
guides.summary: A tickable list of what a household first-aid kit should hold, based on FEMA and Ready.gov lists, plus diabetes-specific items.

guides.title: Hypothermia and frostbite
guides.summary: Signs of hypothermia and frostbite, how to warm someone safely, and what not to do.

guides.title: Over-the-counter medicines: adult label directions
guides.summary: Adult label doses, intervals, daily limits and key warnings for seven common OTC medicines, taken straight from their drug labels.

guides.title: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) and epinephrine
guides.summary: Signs of anaphylaxis, how to use an EpiPen or Auvi-Q, and what to do next.

guides.title: Severe bleeding (Stop the Bleed)
guides.summary: Call 911, press hard on the wound, pack it if it is deep, and use a tourniquet on an arm or leg that will not stop bleeding.

guides.title: Shock
guides.summary: Signs of shock and what to do while you wait for 911: lay them flat, raise the legs, keep them warm.
